questions.question: What is population, and why is a census important?
questions.expected_answer: Population is the number of people living in a particular place. A census is an official count of all the people in a country, usually held about every ten years; in South Africa, it is run by Stats SA, and the 2022 census counted about sixty-two million people. A census is important because governments use the information to plan where to build schools, clinics, roads, houses and water supplies, and businesses use it to plan too.

questions.question: Explain four natural reasons why people live in certain places.
questions.expected_answer: Water is the most important, so many settlements grow next to rivers, lakes and springs, like along the Nile or the Orange and Vaal Rivers. People prefer a pleasant climate that is not too hot, cold, wet or dry. Flat land is easier to build on and farm, and fertile soil helps grow food. Natural resources such as wood, minerals and grazing, and natural features such as sheltered bays and defendable hills, also attract people.

questions.question: Explain four human reasons why people live in certain places.
questions.expected_answer: Jobs attract people, as when thousands moved to Johannesburg after gold was found in 1886. Transport and trade matter, so settlements grow at ports, river crossings, railway junctions and road crossings. Services such as schools, hospitals, shops, electricity and water attract people to towns. History and laws, such as apartheid laws that forced people to live in certain areas, and family ties, culture and religion also influence where people live.
